findings.evidence: `RegularityConditions.lean:153-159` defines `SectorCompatible` with `angle_rational`; `RegularityConditions.lean:170-171` applies it under `< 0`; roadmap `Suggested.lean:108-110` and `README.md:186-187` say condition (B) is for poles of order `> 1`, with the simple-pole case first.
findings.fix: Restrict this clause to higher-order poles, e.g. `meromorphicOrderAt f (γ t₀) < -1`, or make the rational/Laurent compatibility requirement conditional on the presence of a nonzero coefficient of order `> 1`.
findings.issue: The interior clause triggers on every pole `meromorphicOrderAt f (γ t₀) < 0`, so a simple on-curve pole forces `SectorCompatible.angle_rational` even though the simple-pole case is handled without condition (B).

findings.evidence: `RegularityConditions.lean:174` applies `SectorCompatible` under `< 0`; roadmap `README.md:180-187` separates the simple-pole/half-residue case from condition (B), which handles higher-order Laurent cancellation.
findings.fix: Use the same higher-order gate at the basepoint, e.g. require `meromorphicOrderAt f (γ a) < -1` before imposing `SectorCompatible`.
findings.issue: The basepoint clause has the same over-strong trigger: a simple pole at `γ a` must satisfy rational-angle `SectorCompatible`, excluding valid simple-pole endpoint/join cases from the intended theorem API.

summary: `ConditionB` is still stronger than the natural residue-theorem level because it imposes rational-angle sector compatibility on simple poles, even though condition (B) is only needed for higher-order Laurent terms.
